must_remember: Hadrons participate in strong interactions and are divided into Baryons ($qqq$, fermions, half-integral spin) and Mesons ($q\bar{q}$, bosons, integral spin).
Leptons (electron, muon, tau and their neutrinos) are fundamental fermions with spin $1/2$ that do not participate in strong interactions.
Total electric charge ($Q$), baryon number ($B$), and individual lepton numbers ($L_e, L_\mu, L_\tau$) are conserved in all interactions.
Strangeness ($S$) and isospin ($I_3$) are conserved in strong and electromagnetic interactions but can be violated by $\Delta S = \pm 1$ in weak interactions.
Baryons are composed of three quarks ($qqq$) and mesons are composed of a quark-antiquark pair ($q\bar{q}$).
The Gell-Mann-Nishijima formula relates electric charge, isospin, baryon number, and strangeness as $Q = I_3 + \frac{B + S}{2}$.

glossary.meaning: Composite subatomic particles made of quarks that experience the strong nuclear force.
Elementary, point-like fermions that do not undergo strong interactions.
A strictly conserved quantum number assigned +1 to baryons, -1 to antibaryons, and 0 to non-baryons.
A quantum number describing particles containing strange quarks, conserved in strong and electromagnetic interactions.
Force-carrier particles that mediate fundamental interactions (e.g., photon, gluon, $W^{\pm}, Z^0$).
A quantum number related to the strong interaction symmetry between up and down quarks.
